relevance_note: A case report of a child in whom WES "identified the heterozygous variant c.1420A>G (p.Thr474Ala) in exon7 of the TNFAIP3 gene (chr6:138200002)", with AISBL/HA20 discussed as the possible diagnosis.
method_note: Read only the paper, the schema, the rules and the instructions; no other repository file, no web, no git. No script was used (none could be run here), so every value was copied by hand from the Markdown and every span was then re-checked by searching the file (including '3 × 10^9 cells/L', which keeps the literal '^', and 'in exon7' with no space before the 7). The paper has no data tables, so there are no stacked cells to report and no per-patient source column. In-scope people (rule 5, D-22): the 12-year-old boy, his parents, and his eight siblings, who are described as relatives of the boy ("has eight siblings, none of whom have any significant medical history"); the siblings are labelled 'sibling of patient', 'sibling of patient 2' ... 'sibling of patient 8' by the label rules, and the parents 'parent of patient' and 'parent of patient 2' because their sex is not stated. Totals: publications 1, individuals 11, variants 1, phenotypic_features 17 (4 observed, 13 excluded, all for the boy), phenotype_checklist 220 (the 20 checklist features for each of the 11 people). No TNFAIP3 variant is attributed to the parents or siblings and no testing of them is reported, so they get no variant rows. Contradictions found: (1) the boy's TNFAIP3 variant is presented both as a possible cause of AISBL/HA20 and as a "variant of uncertain significance", and the authors conclude "it is unclear whether the detected heterozygous TNFAJP3 variant is causative for the phenotype of our patient"; I therefore recorded no disease label for him and only the authors' own classification of the variant. (2) He is "a product of non-consanguineous parents" (recorded 'no') while the syndrome is described in general as having "an autosomal dominant mode of inheritance". (3) Age at presentation is "12-year-old-boy presented for the first time in April 2017" but the Discussion says he "was nine years old at the time of the first presentation"; I kept the Case presentation age as age at last evaluation and recorded no age at diagnosis. (4) The Discussion spells the gene 'TNFAJP3'; the gene symbol was recorded as printed in the variant sentence. (5) The abstract says the diagnosis "needs further genetic work-up to confirm", so the diagnosis basis is recorded as suspected, not confirmed. Deliberately left as not reported: the variant class (the authors only say the variant "leads to an amino acid exchange" and cite in silico prediction, which is not a stated variant type; the exon is printed as 'exon7'), and the inheritance (no segregation testing: "lack of segregation analysis test of the identified variant for parents and other family members"). Three checklist items for the boy are covered only by broad statements and stay not reported: 'gastrointestinal ulcers or inflammation' (nothing about the gut is reported), 'elevated inflammatory markers (CRP/ESR)' (no CRP or ESR is given anywhere; platelet counts are not inflammatory markers) and 'autoantibodies (ANA/other)' (the only antibody test is "the direct agglutinin test was negative", a red-cell screen, not ANA). Also not used: "Ophthalmology, pediatric-immunology, and pediatric-rheumatology consultations were done, and there were no significant findings" is a normal examination as a whole, so it excludes nothing more specific than what it names (D-27). The 13 excluded rows come from statements about the boy (each excluding only the abnormality it names): "no history of severe bleeding, trauma, or joint involvement", "No paleness or dysmorphic features were observed", "There was no oral or genital ulceration, no organomegaly or lymphadenopathy", "his musculoskeletal system examination was normal", "normal red blood cells, and white blood cell morphology", "all other CBC indices were normal", and "there is no history of bleeding episodes for a long time". For the boy, 'skin lesions (rash, folliculitis, erythema nodosum)' and 'cytopenia (autoimmune)' are observed (vitiligo/hypopigmented patches; thrombocytopenia), 'oral ulcers', 'genital ulcers' and 'lymphoproliferation or lymphadenopathy' are excluded, and the other 15 checklist items are not reported. For the ten relatives every checklist item is not reported: the only statements about them are the group-level "none of whom have any significant medical history" and "There was no family history of ITP, bleeding disorders, malignancies, or sudden deaths", which are normal findings as a whole and name no feature, so they produced no phenotypic_features rows either. Not used: the paper's account of the 14 cases of Zhou et al. and of the Shin et al. case (no individual-level detail), and the general statements about TNFAIP3 variants in the cohort.

treatment_summary.value: IVIG (1 g/kg/day for two consecutive days, and further doses), oral prednisolone 2 mg/kg/day BID for two weeks then tapered over 21 days, Anti-D immunoglobulin (75 µg/kg IV for one dose), rituximab 375 mg/m^2 intravenous weekly for a total of four doses, eltrombopag 50 mg orally once daily increased to 75 mg orally once daily, and topical tacrolimus for the vitiligo; he was considered steroid-resistant and had no response to rituximab or Anti-D
span: We initially treated the patient with IVIG (1 g/kg/day) for two consecutive days followed by oral prednisolone 2 mg/kg/day BID for two weeks and then tapered over 21 days.
As the patient is Rh-positive and the direct agglutinin test was negative, we gave him a single dose of Anti-D immunoglobulin (75 µg/kg IV for one dose), but with no response.
Subsequently, we prescribed rituximab 375 mg/m^2 intravenous weekly for a total of four doses.
Finally, we prescribed eltrombopag 50 mg orally once daily in March 2018.
The dermatologist diagnosed it as vitiligo and prescribed topical tacrolimus.

clinical_diagnosis_basis.value: Suspected by whole-exome sequencing, which identified the heterozygous TNFAIP3 variant; the diagnosis needs further genetic work-up to confirm and the variant is classified as a variant of uncertain significance.
span: The whole-exome sequencing (WES) (performed in Bioscientia Human Genetics) identified the heterozygous variant c.1420A>G (p.Thr474Ala) in exon7 of the TNFAIP3 gene (chr6:138200002)
The initial presentation was chronic ITP with vitiligo, and AISBL was suspected by WES.
Considering the available information, the variant is classified as a variant of uncertain significance.
